citeAs: Rohatgi, S., Qin, Y., Aw, B., Unnithan, N., Kan, M.-Y. (2023). The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics. arXiv:2305.14996.
creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan (Pennsylvania State University; National University of Singapore)
description: ACL OCL is a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It includes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, and structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar. The corpus spans seven decades, containing 73,285 papers published from 1952 to September 2022, alongside 210K figures.
name: ACL OCL
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Topic classification models were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation with 80/20 train/test split. Evaluation metrics included Macro F1, Weighted F1, and Accuracy. The best model (PLM-SPECTER) achieved 66% Macro F1, 68% Weighted F1, and 69% Accuracy. A manual case study on 15 top-cited papers showed 87% accuracy for silver topic labels. Full-text quality was manually assessed on 21 documents, revealing issues with missing sections, footnote merging, and figure/table detection failures.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Topic labels were obtained by crawling published papers from online CL conferences (ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, NAACL 2021) along with their author-submitted topic labels from conference websites. These 2,545 labeled papers (STop dataset) were used to train supervised topic classification models. Silver topic labels for the full OCL corpus were then generated using the best-performing PLM-based model (SPECTER).
rai:dataBiases: The corpus is limited to peer-reviewed CL papers from the ACL Anthology, which may not represent all CL research. English is the dominant language, with many low-resource languages underrepresented. Silver topic labels show bias toward dominant topics (e.g., Machine Translation), leading to higher apparent accuracy on top-cited papers. Topic classification performance is lower than in the news domain (F1 > 80%), reflecting challenges with scientific text. The spike in publications during even years is attributed to conference scheduling (e.g., COLING).
rai:dataCollection: Crawlers were designed to fetch all PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. Metadata is sourced from the website (author-driven, more accurate than PDF extraction). PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed (mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks). The dataset undergoes annual updates by monitoring changes in URLs to identify new additions. The Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) API was used to fetch additional information about OCL papers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata crawled from the ACL Anthology website (https://aclanthology.org/), covering 73,285 conference, journal, and workshop papers in the CL domain.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: OCL is a small-scale collection focused only on peer-reviewed, open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology; it does not include CL papers from arXiv or other sources. Full-text extraction quality is limited by GROBID's constraints, including issues with tables, figures, in-line equations, missing section names, merged paragraphs, and footnote mixing. Only open-source PDF extraction tools were used due to budget constraints. The corpus is an unlabeled resource lacking annotations for specific tasks. Only 16.8% of papers have an arXiv ID. Full-text extraction failures are concentrated in papers from 2000 to 2015.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Silver topic labels were generated for all 73K papers using a trained PLM-based classifier (SPECTER). For topic classification training, 2,036 papers (80%) were randomly selected balanced across topics as training set, and 509 (20%) as test set using 5-fold cross-validation. Automatically detected fields (language, predicted_topic) were added to the dataset schema.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Full-text extraction from PDF files was performed using GROBID. The S2ORC-JSON format was adopted for the full-text schema. Figures and tables were extracted using PDFFigures 2.0. Language detection was performed using a public language detection toolkit (langdetect by Shuyo, 2010) using title and abstract as inputs. PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. The dataset is provided in both CSV and Apache Parquet formats.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which newly added papers from the ACL Anthology are downloaded and processed. New additions are identified by monitoring changes in URLs. The future plan is to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology, ultimately hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ACL OCL advances open science in computational linguistics by providing accessible and standardized data resources, promoting reproducibility in research. It enables analysis of research trends, including the emergence of new topics like "Ethics of NLP" and the representation of low-resource languages. The corpus highlights linguistic disparity, noting that many languages remain underrepresented in the ACL Anthology.
rai:dataUseCases: Temporal topic trend analysis; document-level information extraction; related work generation; figure caption generation; pre-training or fine-tuning scientific large language models; building scientific assistants for the CL domain; section-wise NLP tasks (contribution extraction, future work prediction); citation network analysis; knowledge graph construction; historical language change analysis; multimodal research tasks combining text and figures; bibliographic and metadata analysis.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID (full-text extraction from PDFs); PDFFigures 2.0 (figure and table extraction); langdetect library (language detection); BART-large-MNLI (zero-shot and fine-tuned topic classification); PLM-based classifiers (SciBERT, SPECTER) for silver topic label prediction; Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) API for citation and metadata enrichment.
